text.p: When it comes to gifts for newborn babies, there's a lot more than items in just pink or blue. Scientists agree that even the newest infants respond to black, white and red.
They also respond to and can be calmed by music.

With this in mind, Tyco Toys Inc. has introduced Sesame Street 1-2-3 Melody Keys, an electronic musical toy that is designed to grow with your child. It is recommended for children from birth through age three.

For infants, Sesame Street 1-2-3 Melody Keys plays nursery rhymes continuously for five minutes while lights twinkle. When babies can sit up, they can press any of six Sesame Street characters to play a different tune. Toddlers can add different instrument sounds during the song.

The Big Bird Activity Quilt, also new from Tyco, has 10 different activities such as a mirror, kite, squeaking drum and a teether. There are also textured materials for the baby to explore, such as a satin bow, a clear vinyl pocket and a plush teddy bear. Recommended for ages birth to 18 months, it sells for about $20.

Tyco also has a new toy that allows children to learn a new language as they play. English/Spanish Ernie, for ages 18 months and up, speaks Spanish when his right hand is squeezed and speaks the English translation when his left hand is squeezed. Ernie, the Sesame Street character, speaks 16 phrases in all. The toy sells for about $30.
For more information on Tyco Toys' preschool products, call the company at its New York City headquarters at 212-741-7222.
One Step Ahead is a catalogue filled with new and unusual products for babies.

For children who are afraid of the dark, the catalogue features the Autofade Bedside Light ($34.95). The light fades gradually over 15 minutes. The company says "the gentle automatic dimming effect builds baby's confidence and encourages healthy and restful sleep."

The Sound Beginnings Tape Set ($19.95) exposes infants to six different languages -- Spanish, French, German, Russian, Hebrew and Japanese -- in 15 minute segments. The languages are integrated with music from each culture.

New kits allow parents to make plaster of paris casts of their child's hand or foot. The kits come with non-toxic, non-allergenic and baby-safe materials to make casts of hands or feet of infants ages birth to 12 months. The Hand Casting Kit and Foot Casting Kit cost $19.95 each. My Child's Hand Print kit costs $9.95.

To keep a close eye on your baby, there is the Baby View Monitor ($229.95). The monitor has a small standing camera and transmitter to keep in the baby's room and a television-like screen for parents to watch in the next room or anywhere around the house. The monitor also has a VCR adapter to view tapes and record the baby's activities.
One Step Ahead can be contacted by calling 1-800-274-8440. It also has a catalogue clearance store at the Deerbrook Mall in Deerfield, Ill. (tel. 847-714-1940).
A new book, designed for insatiable science fiction fans is NetSci-Fi, a new addition to the NetBooks series from Wolff New Media.

The book offers a guide to all of the sites on the Internet that would appeal to science fiction fans, such as sci-fi and literature, conventions, movies and television, Star Trek and comics. Cyberpunk devotees can link up with the sites devoted to authors William Gibson, Phillip K. Dick and Bruce Sterling.
The book sells for $22 and can be ordered by calling 1-800-NET-1133 (638-1133) ext. 606.
